startupConfirmations.action: Activated the exact isolated Zen window using Computer Use, then acknowledged the connection startup callback

methodology.mcpApps: Actual Codex app-server plus the shipped MCP App HTML inside an isolated browser host; desktop shell entrypoint schema verified in local Codex code. No automated Codex desktop-shell click claim.
methodology.localPage: Actual Codex with enable_mcp_apps=false and no client UI capability. The production loopback page drives the same connection manager.
methodology.existingFixture: An isolated already-initialized browser profile, a real ordinary tab and HttpOnly cookie; no bridge registration, remote control or extension at first plugin connection.
methodology.freshFixture: An initially empty profile directory and a test-created profiles.ini entry. The actual Zen first-run wizard was completed through Computer Use; this does not claim the plugin creates profiles for a never-started Zen installation.
methodology.onboardingOperator: Computer Use operator simulation, seven effective browser wizard clicks plus the connection UI Continue click. One ineffective accessibility-index click and separate dialog QA are not counted as required product actions.
methodology.nativeOperator: The native restart run required activation of the exact isolated Zen window, explicitly recorded; not a zero-interaction startup claim.
methodology.noGlobalRuntime: The actual MCP child ran with PATH restricted to Windows System32. Installed global Node or PowerShell commands were not available to it.
methodology.testHelpers: Marionette and the native inspection adapter are test facilities, never exposed as production tools.
methodology.rawEvidence: Complete local reports, logs and screenshots are retained in .artifacts and excluded from Git and release packages.
methodology.desktopConfigurationReads: Profile catalog and relevant preference/session flags are read by the desktop helper; a differing caller-side catalog and a preference change after confirmation have regression coverage.

claims.connectionUi: MCP Apps plus a production local-page fallback

limits: Windows x64 package; tested Zen 1.22b / Gecko 155.0.1 and Codex 0.153.4.
MCP Apps rendering depends on the client; the fallback is a browser local page, not the Codex desktop shell.
Some browser startups need actual window activation and an explicit Continue acknowledgement.
First-run browser setup belongs to Zen and remains visible; no automatic theme or default-browser choices.
The unsigned extension is temporary. A normally started profile can need a reviewed restart.
Existing 0.3 manual setup preferences remain user-owned; 0.4 rollback restores only its recorded changes.
No official private @Browser, browser chrome control, native file picker, uploads or closed shadow DOM.
Loopback BiDi has browser-level privileges; it is not an authenticated remote-web endpoint.
In-flight clicks or gestures cannot be undone. Unknown outcomes are never automatically retried.
No actual financial, email or publishing transactions were exercised.
No human pressing the exact same key simultaneously with native typing was arranged.
